skill.name: web-design-guidelines
skill.description: Reviews web UI files against the Vercel Web Interface Guidelines and returns concise file and line findings.
skill.summary: Audit web interfaces against external UI and accessibility guidelines.
skill.author: antfu

security_audit.summary: Two static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and a fenced URL block. The hardcoded GitHub URL is a real low-risk network dependency. The skill also delegates review rules to mutable remote content.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the guidelines to a trusted commit or vendor a local copy so review behavior cannot change without a skill update.
Require user confirmation before WebFetch and treat fetched content as reference material, not higher-priority instructions.

static_findings.snippet: 4. Output findings in the terse `file:line` format

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 contains Markdown inline code for the output format `file:line`. It is prose, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Lines 25-27 are a Markdown fenced block containing a URL. The backticks delimit text and do not execute commands.
The skill instructs WebFetch to retrieve a raw GitHub URL before reviews. This is an intended network dependency and mutable external input.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Remote Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to use fetched content as all review rules and output instructions. A changed remote file could alter behavior during audits.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines require fetching and applying mutable remote instructions. No malicious content is present in the local files.

content.user_title: Review Web Interfaces Against UI Guidelines
content.value_statement: Design reviews are hard to keep consistent across accessibility, UX, and interface rules. This skill applies external Web Interface Guidelines to selected files and reports concise issues.
actual_capabilities: Fetches the current Web Interface Guidelines from the configured GitHub source.
Reviews user-specified UI files or file patterns.
Checks interface code against guideline rules and accessibility expectations.
Reports findings with file and line references.
Asks which files to review when no target is provided.
limitations: Requires network access to retrieve the latest guideline source.
Review quality depends on the remote guideline content.
It does not automatically fix code or run visual regression tests.
It cannot verify behavior that is absent from the provided files.

use_cases.title: Audit a React Interface
use_cases.description: Check component files before merging to catch UI, accessibility, and interaction issues.

use_cases.title: Review Design System Changes
use_cases.description: Evaluate shared components against interface rules before publishing a new package version.

use_cases.title: Validate Product Screens
use_cases.description: Run a concise UX and accessibility review on important pages before release.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one route or page file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review `app/page.tsx` against the Web Interface Guidelines and list concise findings.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Component Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a focused group of shared UI components.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all files in `src/components/**/*.tsx` for accessibility, layout, and interaction guideline issues.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Feature Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Inspect a complete product area before handoff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review `app/settings/**` and focus on form usability, error states, keyboard access, and responsive behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Before Release
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a deeper review on high-impact surfaces.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review `app/dashboard/**` and `src/components/data-table/**`. Prioritize release-blocking UI, accessibility, and UX issues.

output_examples.output: A concise list of issues with file and line references, grouped by guideline impact.

output_examples.input: Check accessibility for the settings page.
output_examples.output: Findings that focus on labels, keyboard access, focus order, contrast, and error messaging.
A prioritized review of blocking interface issues and smaller polish items.

best_practices: Provide exact files or narrow patterns for a focused review.
Review fetched guideline content as untrusted reference material.
Run automated tests and visual checks alongside the skill review.
anti_patterns: Asking it to review an entire repository without scope.
Treating remote guideline text as higher priority than system or developer instructions.
Using findings as the only accessibility validation step.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews web interface files against the Vercel Web Interface Guidelines.

faq.question: Does it change files?
faq.answer: No. It reports issues and line references only.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to fetch current guidelines before each review.

faq.question: Can it audit accessibility?
faq.answer: It can identify accessibility issues covered by the guideline source.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe to use?
faq.answer: It has a runtime network dependency. Review or pin the remote guideline source for stricter security.
